_comment: Tells somebody when ../detectors/api-latency.json raises an issue.
Its own workflow, for the reason waitlist-submit-failed.json gives:
one file, one detector, keeps apply.sh's refusal meaningful.
regression_event and a team target, both copied from the waitlist
rule because both were SEEN there and a metric monitor behaves the
same way. It raises ONE issue and reopens it on every later breach,
so first_seen_event alone fires once in the monitor's life. And its
issue is owned by team:onlooker, so issue_owners with an AllMembers
fallthrough was seen to email nobody.
ONL-49 also asked for an API failure-rate rule. There isn't one, on
purpose. Sentry's failure_rate() counts every non-ok status, and over
the 7 days to 2026-10-27 it read 70% for the API with no 5xx at all in
30 days: 6,500 404s from scanners and 179 401s. Narrowed to 5xx it
would repeat api-faults.json, since every 5xx the API returns is a
reported fault and already emails, so it was left out rather than
tuned until it was quiet.
SEEN TO DELIVER: with the detector's threshold lowered to 100ms by a
one-off apply at 2026-10-28T01:56Z (the trailing-hour p95 was 264ms),
the monitor opened ONLOOKER-API-6, this workflow fired at 02:00:18Z,
and the email reached a team member. The threshold was put back to
2000 by a full apply at 02:07Z. To repeat the test, apply a lowered
copy through SENTRY_DETECTORS_DIR and this file alone, so the
committed threshold is never the one that changes.
